analysis: Examined docs/provider/troubleshooting.md base/head and the ProviderLoop+Autopilot.swift patch. The doc change (head lines 3, 134, 167-169) is operator guidance. Line 134 documents bounded lifecycle drain waits (10 s for a session, 15 s per unload at shutdown) and says --force interrupts only unfinished work. Lines 167-169 document automatic retry of explicitly selected models when memory frees. Per the doc, eviction is limited to idle, non-selected models with no Autopilot hold, pin or lease, and must meet Autopilot's minimum dwell and idle time. The doc also covers the restart-needed status for a changed enabled_models filter. None of this changes encryption, attestation, authorization or data-exposure controls (TB-002, TB-011, T-053). The doc text adds no prompt or secret logging. The code change (head line 213) adds noteSelectedModelUnloaded(victim, by: command) after a successful Autopilot eviction unload. This is availability and scheduling bookkeeping, not a security control. Integration should check whether the retry/eviction loop could churn or thrash models or fight Autopilot (availability, T-029-adjacent). The implementations of noteSelectedModelUnloaded and the retry scheduler are not in this batch, so the doc's eviction constraints are unverified. The coordinator still controls routing, and providers are adversarial but self-owned for local scheduling. No concrete regression was identified.
